description: Between two chairs or on parallel bars, your strict dip number tells the truth about the tendons that guard your shoulders. Most guys wreck the test - and their shoulders - with the same five mistakes. Here is the strict version, the cables it loads, and how to build pressing power without paying for it in shoulder pain.

scenes.narration: Set up on bars, | or two strong chairs. | Grip firm. | Arms locked out. | Shoulders set down. | Lower yourself slowly | until your chest | reaches bar level, | upper arms parallel | to the floor. | Press back up | to a full lockout. | That is one rep. | No bouncing | at the bottom. | No kicking | with your legs. | Count every strict rep | until your form | starts to break. | That number | is your dip max. | Write it down. | At the end, | I will tell you | what it says | about the cables | guarding your shoulders.

scenes.label: THE LINE BETWEEN SHAKY AND SOLID PRESSING
scenes.narration: Here is the line. Fifteen strict dips is where shaky pressing becomes solid pressing. Under five, the shoulder cables are untrained, and untrained is a starting point, not a verdict. Five to twelve means the system is building and the lockout is starting to feel automatic instead of desperate. Over twenty, you own pressing power that most bench press regulars cannot match with their own bodyweight, because their strength lives in one groove and yours lives in your own frame. Notice what the strict rules did to your number. Full depth and full lockout probably halved your usual total. The missing half was bounce, momentum and half-finished reps. Your tendons never got paid for that half, which is why it never made you stronger.
scenes.sub: under 5: untrained cables - over 20: serious press power

beats.text: FOUR SMALL CABLES GUARD THE JOINT

beats.label: OF THE LOAD LANDS AT FULL DEPTH

beats.text: CONTROL THE BOTTOM, OWN THE DIP

scenes.narration: Look inside the shoulder, because the dip is really two exercises stacked together. The big muscles you know, chest and triceps, drive the press through their tendons. But underneath them, four small muscles called the rotator cuff run their own tendons across the joint, and their only job is to keep the ball of your arm bone centered in its shallow socket while the big engines pull. At the bottom of a dip, your shoulder is stretched into its most vulnerable position, loaded with most of your bodyweight, and the guard crew is working at its absolute limit. This is why the bottom two inches of the dip decide everything. Control them, and the exercise builds some of the most durable shoulders in bodyweight training. Crash through them, and the same exercise becomes the one that hurts people. The dip is not dangerous. The uncontrolled bottom is. Think of it this way: the chest and triceps are the engine of the dip, but the rotator cuff is the steering. An engine without steering does not go fast for long. It just crashes sooner.

Here is the science of the sore shoulder. The stress on your shoulder cables is not set by how much you weigh. It is set by position. When your shoulders roll forward at the bottom of the dip, the load concentrates onto a few small structures at the front of the joint. When you keep the shoulders pulled down and slightly back, chest open, the same bodyweight spreads across the whole system, muscle and tendon sharing the bill. Same guy, same weight, completely different stress, decided entirely by two inches of shoulder position. This is also why wall slides and similar cuff work appear in every serious shoulder program. They train the guard crew to hold position under fatigue. A dip performed with set shoulders is a tendon builder. The identical dip with rolled shoulders is a tendon tax. Your test graded your strength. Your form decides what the training does to you.

lines: You need a chair and a floor.
beats.title: THE LIGHT ADVANTAGE

scenes.narration: Now your advantage. | Dips charge full price: | your whole bodyweight, | every single rep. | A heavy guy | cannot do one | without bands, | boxes, assistance. | You can start today, | full range, | full lockout, | nothing but chairs. | And because you are light, | you collect more reps | before fatigue wins. | More strict reps | means more tendon dose | per session, | per week, | per month. | The heavy guy | is still learning | to hold himself up. | You are already | building the cables.

Before we train, understand the ladder you are climbing. At the bottom are bench dips, feet on the floor, where your legs carry part of the load and the shoulder cables learn the pattern cheaply. The middle rung is the full dip you tested today, full bodyweight, full depth. The top rungs add load slowly, a book-filled backpack at a time, because tendon tissue adapts to small increases and rebels against jumps. The mistake almost everyone makes is skipping rungs, jumping from five shaky reps to a loaded belt because a video told them to. Each rung exists to give the cables a few weeks at a load they can rebuild against. Climb one rung at a time and your shoulders will feel boringly healthy for years. Skip rungs and the same exercise becomes a countdown. The ladder is not slow. The ladder is the speed limit of collagen itself.
Now press with me. Controlled down, chest to bar level, strong lockout. Twenty-five seconds on, sixty-five seconds off, four rounds. Quality over count. Go.

beats.text: SLOW DOWN, FULL UP, SHOULDERS SET

scenes.narration: Here are the five mistakes destroying your shoulder tendons on dips. First, dropping fast and bouncing out of the bottom. That crash loads the guard crew at its weakest point with zero control. Lower for a full two seconds instead. Second, skipping the lockout. The top of the rep is where the triceps tendon finishes its work, and half-finished reps build half-finished cables. Third, letting the shoulders roll forward as you tire, which spikes the stress exactly where you can least afford it. Fourth, swinging the legs to steal momentum, which turns a shoulder exercise into a circus trick. Fifth, adding a weight belt before you own fifteen strict bodyweight reps. Load magnifies whatever your form already is. And one serious note: if your shoulders ever ache sharply during dips, stop, and if that ache persists, see a professional. Tendons reward patience and punish pride.

So, your number. Under five strict reps: your pressing cables are untrained, and this is the band where progress comes embarrassingly fast, sometimes a rep a week. Five to twelve: the system is building, lockouts are getting honest, and the shoulders are learning their job. Fifteen and beyond: your pressing is solid by any bodyweight standard, and slow added load becomes your next tool. Over twenty: you own press power most people never build. Whatever your number is, put it in the comments. Just the number. In thirty days we set up the bars again and count, and your shoulders will report what the month did. And remember, depth is part of the number. Fifteen strict reps at full depth outrank twenty-five shallow ones everywhere except in ego.
Thirty days from now, same bars, same strict rules, more reps. Subscribe so you do not miss the retest, and bring your strong shoulders. This is {channel}. Train the cable.

title: 5 dip max Mistakes That Are Destroying Your shoulder tendons
